name: Quad stretch (standing)
summary: Standing, hold one ankle behind you and draw the heel toward the buttock, knees together.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, one hand on a wall. Bend the working knee, hold the ankle behind you, and gently pull the heel toward the buttock with the knee pointing down. Hold.
brief: One hand on a wall. Bend the working knee, hold the ankle behind you, and gently pull the heel toward the buttock with the knee pointing down.
why: The knee angle from the side shows how far the heel has come up, so the timer runs only in the stretch position.
tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, release slowly.
progression: Tuck the pelvis under to deepen; no wall.
regression: Hold the trouser leg or a strap; lie on your side.
contraindications: Kneecap pain in the bent knee, or cramp in the hamstring.

faults.label: Knee drifting forward or out
faults.cue: Point the knee at the floor
faults.tip: Keep the two knees side by side. The stretch comes from the hip extending, not the knee flaring.

faults.label: Arching the back
faults.tip: Squeeze the buttock and tuck the tailbone under — that is where the stretch deepens.

faults.label: Holding the foot too hard
faults.tip: Pulling the heel hard into the backside compresses the kneecap. A firm stretch is enough.

faults.label: Leaning forward
faults.tip: Folding forward slackens the hip flexor and the stretch disappears.

guide.surface: Firm floor and something to hold.

points.t: Heel to buttock, knee pointing at the floor beside the other knee.
Tall, pelvis tucked, light hand on the wall.
